'''Alessandra Carbone''' is an  Italian [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]]. She is a professor in the computer science department of the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ihes.fr/~carbone/index.html|title=Analytical Genomics|website=www.ihes.fr|access-date=2019-03-16}}</ref> Since 2009 she has headed the laboratory of computational and [[quantitative biology]].<ref name=ibps>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ibps.upmc.fr/fr/Recherche/umr-7238/genomique-analytique|work=IBPS |title= Génomique analytique|access-date=2019-03-16}}</ref>

==Career==
She gained her PhD in mathematics in 1993 at the [[Graduate Center of the City University of New York]], supervised by [[Rohit Jivanlal Parikh]],<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=35646}}</ref> after which she took up a post doctoral post at the [[Paris Diderot University]] until 1995 when she took a position at the [[Technical University of Vienna]] until 1996. She has taught computer science at the [[Paris 12 Val de Marne University]] and the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]]. She is currently a professor at Sorbonne University, previously known as Pierre and Marie Curie University

==Recognition==
Carbone is a senior member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]] and received the [[Irène Joliot-Curie Prize]] in 2010.<ref name=ibps/>
She is also a recipient in 2012 of the {{ill|Grammaticakis-Neumann Prize|de}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/activite/prix/laureat_grammaticakis_bio.pdf|title=Prix Grammaticakis-Neumann (Biologie intégrative)|publisher=French Academy of Sciences|access-date=2024-01-27}}</ref> and the [[Legion of Honour]] in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scai.sorbonne-universite.fr/public/profiles/view/7e32d291c8c4d977f7fc/27|title=Alessandra Carbone|publisher=Sorbonne Center for Artificial Intelligence|access-date=2024-01-27}}</ref>
